Calibrate the drift screens on data known not to have drifted

Source: R/scan_adjust.R
drftcal.Rd

cpsdrft() flags a column when a Kolmogorov-Smirnov, chi-square or population-stability screen fires. How often that happens when nothing has changed is the false-alarm rate of the screen on this capsule, and it depends on the columns, their sizes and alpha. This estimates it by splitting the same data at random into two halves n times and running the screens on the halves, which is the null of “a re-fetch of identical data”. A capsule whose screens fire on 30 percent of identical re-fetches needs a smaller alpha or fewer screened columns before a drift verdict means anything.

Usage

drftcal(data, n = 50L, alpha = 0.01, seed = 1L, ...)

Arguments

data

The capsule's data frame.

n

Whole number, default 50: the number of random half-splits.

alpha

Number in (0, 1), default 0.01: the significance level passed to cpsdrft().

seed

Integer or NULL, default 1: the seed for the splits.

...

Further arguments to cpsdrft(), such as psithr, psiminn, bins or idelvls.

Value

A list of class rmbl_drift_calibration: columns (a data frame of column and falsealarmrate, the share of splits on which it was flagged), anyflag (share of splits with at least one flag), alpha, n, and alphafam (alpha divided by the number of columns: the Bonferroni per-screen level that would hold the family-wise false-alarm rate at alpha). The print method lists the columns that fired.

Details

Each split draws floor(nrow(data) / 2) rows at random as the reference and uses the rest as the current table, then runs cpsdrft on the pair. A column's false-alarm rate is the share of splits on which it was flagged; anyflag is the share of splits on which any column was. Each half has half the rows of the real data, so the rates describe a comparison at that size: smaller samples make the p-value screens less sensitive, and the PSI screen only counts once both halves reach psiminn rows.

The splits are drawn under seed and the caller's random number stream is restored afterwards (seed = NULL uses and advances the current stream instead). Run time is about n times one cpsdrft() call; a progress bar is shown in an interactive session.

Errors: data not a data frame with at least four rows; n not a whole number of at least 1; any error from cpsdrft().

See also

cpsdrft, scanadj.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(a = rnorm(400), b = sample(letters[1:4], 400, TRUE))
drftcal(d, n = 10)
#> Drift screens on 10 identical re-fetches (alpha = 0.01)
#>   at least one column flagged: 0% of re-fetches
#>   no column fired on identical data
#>   per-screen alpha for a family-wise 0.01: 0.005

# a stricter level, and the per-column rates
cal <- drftcal(d, n = 10, alpha = 0.001)
cal$columns
#>   column falsealarmrate
#> a      a              0
#> b      b              0

try(drftcal(d[1:3, ]))
#> Error : `data` must be a data frame with at least four rows
